# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s140d, seat B) | **KS-720 round 1 (PR #871)** — `a821bd0aa` → `6845b1cd3` (authentication on `/link` and `/unlink` only, never the four public routes, plus `null` instead of `undefined` on the unlink write; full `services/auth` suite 43 files / 595 tests / 0 failed) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Gate queued — this row scores the build. **The red-proof PAIR is correctly designed and it said why neither alone would do:** tamper A (authentication removed) reds 5 and leaves the two public-route CONTROLS green; tamper B (`null` reverted to `undefined`, authentication left intact) reds ONLY the write cell — *"zero UPDATEs means the handler returned success having persisted nothing"* — with CONTROL 3 green. Under A the write cells red as COLLATERAL, since without `req.user` the handler never reaches its write, which is exactly why A alone could not have proved the second defect fixed. Each tamper undone by inverse edit, byte-identity by sha256, porcelain 0, **and the suite re-run green afterwards to prove the restores were real rather than merely hashed.** It named its own two limits (no end-to-end probe through the real gateway; `walletAddress` absent from the encryption map is a READ, not a driven test) and left `userRepo.updateUser` untouched because its `undefined` skip is shared semantics with a deferred defect — fixing the caller instead. |
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura SEAT A KS-921 PASS WITH FINDINGS (#870, TIER 1)** — `191bc1cc9` on `a821bd0aa` (2026-09-06 21:15→21:36 AEST, ~35 min; own `clone --shared` plus a second clone at the base; **leg 13 driven END-TO-END against its own bare remote** — a good corpus pushes, one deleted re-link is REFUSED and the remote holds no refs) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It found a FALSE CLEAN in a guard whose entire purpose is to prevent one.** F-1: the corpus grep is case-sensitive while Dockerfile keywords are case-insensitive by specification, so `Copy --from=shared-builder` silently leaves the class and the guard prints `OK — 1 of 1 clean` over a corpus of two with the second broken in both clauses — surviving STRICT mode, invisible to the vacuous-green protection (which only fires on an ENTIRELY empty class), and with the derived count shrinking in step so no figure looks wrong. Plus two more Majors, both false BLOCKS on a clause that blocks today: only the FIRST `USER` per stage is recorded (so root → link → drop-privileges is rejected with a message that is factually wrong about the file), and the re-link regex rejects `ln -sf` — "the likeliest of all my false blocks to be written by a real author". It verified all eleven brief claims, showed the suite notices an over-firing guard in both clauses, and **published TWO instrument corrections of its own**: a double-quoted perl tamper whose variable the shell expanded to empty, so neither tamper landed and both runs still reported 18 passed (caught only because a verification grep printed nothing — every tamper now carries a sha256 landing assertion), and a base measured with `git archive` where the fixture needs a real `.git`. |

> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships

> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)

> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."
